# Appeal of Denial – Total Ankle Replacement (CPT 27702)

**Governing Policy:** Cigna Medical Coverage Policy 0285 Total Ankle Arthroplasty — https://static.cigna.com/assets/chcp/pdf/coveragePolicies/medical/mm_0285_coveragepositioncriteria_total_ankle_arthroplasty.pdf

**Member:** Sawyer Alvarez
**Member ID:** W635441117
**Reference Number:** POC-A1F3D3C000-86797
**Date of Denial Notice:** 2026-08-11
**Plan:** Cigna (Commercial/ACA), Ohio

To Whom It May Concern:

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization request for a total ankle replacement (CPT 27702), which Cigna denied on 2026-08-11 on the grounds that the procedure does not meet the plan's medical necessity criteria. My surgeon, Dr. Duval, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I am asking Cigna to reconsider this decision based on the plan's own published policy and the records already submitted.

## Why I believe the denial should be reversed

Cigna's own coverage policy states that a total ankle arthroplasty using an:

> "Food and Drug Administration (FDA)- approved/cleared device* is considered medically necessary as an alternative to ankle arthrodesis when ALL of the following criteria have been met:"

The policy then lists those criteria as follows:

> " is function-limiting at short distances (e.g., walking less than ¼ mile, limiting activity to two city blocks, the equivalent to walking the length of a shopping mall) for at least three (3) months duration  interferes with the ability to carry out age appropriate activities of daily living and/or demands of employment • failure of at least six months of conservative therapy (i.e., anti-inflammatory medications, orthotic devices, activity modification, physical therapy) • individual has NONE of the following contraindications to total ankle arthroplasty:"

My records show the following, which I believe meet these criteria:

**Function-limiting at short distances for at least three months.** My chart documents that I ambulate with an antalgic gait and am limited to two blocks, which matches the plan's own example of "limiting activity to two city blocks." This limitation has been present throughout my 12-month history of progressive ankle pain, well beyond the three-month threshold in the policy.

**Failure of at least six months of conservative therapy.** My records document 8 months of NSAID use with inadequate relief, a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-29 that gave only two weeks of partial relief, and 10 weeks (18 visits) of supervised physical therapy from 2026-04-18 to 2026-06-27. This combination of medication, injection, and physical therapy is the same type of conservative treatment the policy describes, and it extended well past six months.

**Absence of contraindications.** My records specifically note no active infection and no untreated substance use. [If the plan's contraindication list includes additional items beyond what is quoted above, please advise so my surgeon and I can address them directly.]

**Interference with daily activities or employment.** [Additional documentation regarding the specific impact of my ankle condition on daily activities and/or work duties can be provided if needed to complete the record on this point.]

I also want to note that several of the criteria cited in connection with this denial — including the language about "moderate to severe ankle pain secondary to failure of an implanted device" and "Revision surgery may be necessary in the presence of failed arthroplasty" — appear in the policy under the section for **revision** total ankle arthroplasty. My requested procedure, CPT 27702, is a primary total ankle replacement, not a revision of a prior implant, so I ask that my request be evaluated under the primary-arthroplasty criteria quoted above, which is the section the policy identifies as governing when a device is used "as an alternative to ankle arthrodesis."

Weight-bearing radiographs from 2026-06-02 also document tibiotalar joint space obliteration with subchondral cysts, and my exam findings include positive provocative testing and pain-limited range of motion, all consistent with the degree of ankle arthritis this procedure is intended to treat.

## What I am asking

I am asking Cigna to reconsider this denial in light of the criteria quoted directly from Cigna's own Coverage Policy 0285 and the clinical documentation already submitted by Dr. Duval's office. If any additional records are needed to complete this review, please let me know specifically what is missing so my surgeon's office can provide it.

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-07, though I recognize my denial letter is the authoritative source for this deadline. I will submit this appeal through my.cigna.com and/or by calling the number on my member ID card, and I will also send it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter.

Thank you for reconsidering my request.

Sincerely,

______________________________
Sawyer Alvarez
Member ID: W635441117
[Address]
[Phone number]
[Email address]
Date: [Date]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
